marta: Heads-up — non-chat embeddings/reranker endpoint p50 jumped ~18% after the recent kernel selector tweak. Spotted correlation with top-10 heavy queries where avg seq len ~160.
sam: Ugh. Which kernel change? the attention fusion landing last week?
marta: Yeah, merge: kernel-selector now prefers fused-attn-fast by default. Perf timeline: week before change p50=42ms, today p50=50ms, p95 up from 190ms -> 260ms. Links: https://console.redwood.ai/perf/alerts/emb-rank-1938
leo: Can you paste a sample profile? kv-cache hit ratio? sounds like small-batch KV thrash.
marta: quick snippets from profiler (5m window):
```
endpoint: reranker-nonchat-v3
avg_batch_size: 4.1
avg_tokens_per_request: 158
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.38
kernel_choice: fused-attn-fast (70%), kv_friendly (30%)
context_switches: +22%
```
nora: low kv cache hit rate would explain extra memory bandwidth and kernel switch overhead. fused-attn-fast is not optimized for fragmented kvcache footprints.
sam: Agree. Also our batch assembly heuristic currently uses token_budget_target=4096 and batch_max_wait_ms=6 which prioritized filling by requests count rather than token slices.
marta: Proposed quick experiment:
- reduce token_budget_target -> 2048 for reranker endpoints
- increase batch_max_wait_ms -> 12ms (give assembly more time to form homogeneous token groups)
- prefer kernel affinity: prefer kv_friendly for avg seq len > 120
I can roll a canary.
leo: +1. Another idea: token-slicing during assembly — if a single request has huge token length we cap slice to 320 to avoid dominating batch. That should stabilize kvcache locality.
perf-bot: perf-scan: schedule job rerank-compare-193850 at 11:10 UTC, sampling 10k requests across prod traffic (read-only) :white_check_mark:
nora: Also add a tracing tag so we can see kernel switch rate per batch. Right now we only observe endpoint-level metrics.
sam: How about a fallback policy: if fused-attn-fast latency > 1.25x baseline for last 5m, route batches to kv_friendly automatically.
marta: I like fallback. Will add rollout strategy: canary to 3 pods in us-west for 1 hour, compare p50/p95 and kv_hit_rate.
infra-bot: deploy plan:
- config: /configs/rerank/assembly/experiment-193850.json
- rollout: canary 3 pods -> wait 1h -> promote
- rollback: manual if p95 increases > 10% or error_rate > 0.1%
sam: small nit: metric calculation should use request-weighted p50 (not pod-avg) to avoid skew from low-traffic pods.
leo: I'll add a dashboard panel: kernel-switch-rate, kv_hit_rate, token_budget_utilization, batch_homogeneity_ratio.
marta: I'll push the canary now and post results here. expecting initial improvement in p95 and kv_hit_rate, maybe slight p50 cost from increased wait_ms.
nora: If we don't see improvement, next step is to add a kernel microbenchmark that simulates our non-chat embed shapes and run on both kernels to confirm theoretical perf.
marta: Thanks all. kicking off canary -> job id rerank-compare-193850
perf-bot: job started: rerank-compare-193850 (sampler=10k, window=30m)

marta: Quick interim: canary live in us-west; early stats after 10k samples: p50=48ms (down from 50), p95=210ms (down from 260), kv_hit_rate=0.62 (up from 0.38)
sam: Nice, looks promising. Keep watchers on kernel-switch-rate.
leo: If stable after 1h we should promote and then do a follow-up to optimize token_budget_target per-tenant (some clients send very long vectors).
nora: Filing follow-ups: small benchmark harness + per-tenant budget config PR. I'll create tickets.
marta: Added ticket: https://redwood.ai/issue/ENG-PLT-1942 — will attach canary logs.
perf-bot: job completed: rerank-compare-193850 status=success samples=10000 duration=33m
marta: Great work. I'll open a brief doc with the assembly heuristics we tuned and the rollback criteria. :thumbsup:
sam: Thanks — nice fast experiment loop. :rocket:
